|    | Needs assessment: What is the problem?                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Input/ activity: What is the solution?                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Impact                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|---:|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 18 | Address energy efficiency and gender inequality issues. Provide better financial and information access to vulnerable children and women through affordable cleaner energy. · Significant amount of household income is spent on heating in ger area household · Poor families face significant financial burden due to high fuel costs, but, resulting in paying highest utility cost. · Air pollution is a major cause of illness among children, pregnant women and elderly people. | Output: 30,000 households insulated with energy efficient windows and doors. Provide better financial and information access to vulnerable children and women through affordable cleaner energy. · Health and safety hazards are reduced due to replacement of old heating systems with new ones. Reduced expenditure on heating from poor households, which can be diverted to education and job creation. Improved respiratory health in local communities. Increased participation of women in green businesses. | Impact: Healthier children and women with reduced risk of respiratory diseases. Improved air quality. Improved respiratory health in local communities. Increased participation of women in green businesses. Increased awareness of climate change among the community. Improved livelihoods of poor households. |
